0.text: Speed is your biggest conversion lever for local business.

1.text: Your contact page is where curious visitors become paying customers
and most local business sites get it wrong.
Put your phone number, address, and a short form above the fold.
Promise a response time you can actually hit.

2.text: Place your number in three spots on the contact page: the header, a hero block near the top
and a sticky mobile bar at the bottom of the screen.
If you answer calls from 8 AM to 6 PM Monday through Friday, say so in plain text.

3.text: Phone (we will call back today)" tells the visitor what happens next.
Replace the generic "Submit" button with action language: "Get My Quote, " "Request A Callback
Buttons that describe the outcome convert better than buttons that describe the mechanic.

4.text: We serve homes within 25 miles of Greenville, SC" beats a vague "Servicing the Upstate area.
Specifics build trust and pull in the right leads.
Tell visitors exactly when they will hear back.
We reply to every message within 2 business hours
8 AM to 6 PM Monday through Friday" is a promise you can hit.

5.text: If you cannot answer in two hours, change the promise to four.
Your contact page should be one click away from every page on your site.
Put a "Contact" link in the main navigation, in the footer
and as a button at the end of every service page and blog post.

If you use a chat widget, set realistic hours and an offline message.
A chat bubble that says "Online Now" but never responds is worse than no chat at all.
